newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian police foil attempt to storm Pizza Hut.
newsitem.headline: Indian police foil attempt to storm Pizza Hut.

text.p: Police in the southern Indian city of Bangalore said on Wednesday they had foiled an attempt by activists opposed to foreign multinationals to storm a fast food restaurant run by U.S. chain Pizza Hut.

Police said they arrested at least 40 protesters of the regional Akhila Karnataka Yuvaka Parishad (All Karanataka Youth Council) when they tried to break in during a protest on the birth anniversary of nationalist leader Mahatma Gandhi.

Police rushed to overpower the volunteers who raised slogans in the fashionable Cunningham Road against Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and fast food outlets Kentucky Fried Chicken (KFC) and Pizza Hut, both owned by PepsiCo.
Bangalore has welcomed global computer giants with open arms, but socialist protestors have on several occasions targeted firms they say hurts the interests of local farmers and Indian culture.

Activists of a militant farmers' organisation ransacked KFC's first restaurant in Bangalore this year on January 30, the anniversary of the 1948 assassination of Gandhi, five months after he led India to freedom from British rule.
Women's groups, regional hardliners and right-wing Hindu organisations are currently leading a protest against a Miss World beauty contest scheduled to be held in Bangalore in November this year.

Police said the farmers' association had no links with the Kannada language chauvinists who tried to break into Pizza Hut. Kannada is the main language in the state of Karnataka, whose state capital is Bangalore.
Pizza Hut and KFC entered India under a five-year-old economic reform programme that welcomes foreign investors.
